processing: A tea plant variety rather than a finished tea. As with most green tea plants, the leaf would be fixed, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: An early-sprouting variety, so it comes in early in the spring; no picking standard is documented.
appearance_dry: Not documented for the finished tea; expect a medium-sized green leaf typical of its class.
appearance_liquor: Not documented; green tea of this kind is normally a clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Medium-sized leaves, in line with its medium-leaf classification.
taste_profile: No dedicated tasting notes are documented; a general green tea profile of vegetal freshness and light sweetness is the safest expectation.

brewing.notes: General advice for green tea, not specific to this variety.

vintage_note: This variety is not usually sold under its own name; it is grown as a companion plant within regional gardens. Tea made from it would, as is usual for green tea, be sold as the current spring harvest.
description:
Paiqi Zhong is a tea plant variety, known by the formal name Camellia sinensis cv. Paiqizhong. It is listed under Guangxi here, although its origin details are thin.

Botanically it is a seed-propagated, small-tree type with medium leaves. It sprouts early, is diploid, and grows tall and upright with moderate branching.

It tends to be planted as a companion variety in tea gardens, which means you are more likely to drink it blended into a regional tea than to meet it on its own. No dedicated tasting notes are documented.

If a seller names it, ask what the leaf was made into and where it was grown.
history: Little is documented about this variety beyond its botanical description: its first recording and any breeding or selection history remain unclear.
